title: HTTP JSON API for memory: /api/v1/memory* on the authenticated pipeline, with superadmin oversight (+ OpenAPI)
priority_note: Bridges the domain (28.2) to the MCP layer (28.4); must reuse the existing auth/witness pipeline exactly. Also carries operator oversight (superadmin) since loopctl has no web UI.

background.reference: GitHub issue #307; mirrors the knowledge_* controllers and the full :authenticated router pipeline. Enhanced-review round 1 applied: subject derivation reconciled with the role floor; operator oversight moved from a (nonexistent) LiveView to a superadmin API path; OpenAPI-operations location corrected; cross-subject isolation test added.
background.includes: The MCP tools (US-28.4) call the Phoenix /api/v1 API, not the context directly, so memory inherits tenant resolution, role gating, and witness/chain-of-custody. The full :authenticated pipeline (lib/loopctl_web/router.ex) is ExtractApiKey → ResolveApiKey → SetTenant → SeedTenantMetadata → Impersonate → RequireAuth → RateLimiter → ValidateWitnessHeader → CheckCustodyHalt → UpdateLastSeen (do not rely on an abbreviated subset).

story.as_a: a loopctl API consumer (an agent via MCP, or a direct client) and, for oversight, a superadmin
story.i_want_to: call REST endpoints to write, recall, list, and delete my own scoped memory, and (as superadmin) list/delete memory across subjects within a tenant
story.so_that: agents use memory over the same governed transport as the knowledge and story APIs, and a human operator retains visibility + delete control without a web UI

rationale: loopctl's MCP server is a thin HTTP client over /api/v1, so memory must live there to inherit tenant resolution, role gating, and the witness/custody layer instead of re-implementing them. Because loopctl is agent-native (no human web UI), Cole Medin's 'operator visibility + delete' requirement is met by a superadmin-scoped API oversight path rather than a LiveView.

acceptance_criteria.description: LoopctlWeb.MemoryController + MemoryJSON view expose, under scope "/api/v1" on the :authenticated pipeline: POST /api/v1/memory (remember), POST /api/v1/memory/recall (semantic recall), GET /api/v1/memory (list, limit/offset + total_count meta), DELETE /api/v1/memory/:id (forget).

Scope (tenant_id + subject_id) is derived from the resolved API key per US-28.1 AC-28.1.4 (agent_id for agent keys, else api_key.id), NOT from the request body; any tenant_id/subject_id in the body is ignored. If subject_id cannot be resolved the request is rejected with a deterministic 4xx (never a null-scoped write). Role note: agent is the FLOOR role, so 'authenticated' is the effective gate for own-memory operations — the real boundary is (tenant_id, subject_id), not role; document this so it is not misread as a privilege gate.

The full :authenticated plug chain applies; a custody-halted key cannot write memory (CheckCustodyHalt), a missing/invalid witness header is rejected consistently with other write endpoints (ValidateWitnessHeader), and the write path is subject to RateLimiter.

Superadmin oversight (replaces the web inspector): a superadmin-role key MAY list all subjects' memories within its tenant (GET /api/v1/memory?all_subjects=true or an /api/v1/admin/memory route) and delete any memory in the tenant. Non-superadmin keys are strictly confined to their own subject_id; requesting all_subjects as a non-superadmin is ignored/403.

recall responses carry the pinned shape/meta from US-28.2 AC-28.2.6 (results + meta.fallback/reason); list carries offset/limit/total_count; errors use the API's standard error envelope; no endpoint imposes a silent hard cap.

OpenAPI: operation macros are declared IN LoopctlWeb.MemoryController via use OpenApiSpex.ControllerSpecs (collected by Paths.from_router/1), and request/response SCHEMAS are added under lib/loopctl/api_spec/. The endpoints render at /swaggerui and the existing openapi_test passes with no 'No operation spec defined' warning for the new actions.

test_cases.name: remember + recall round-trip over HTTP within tenant/subject scope
preconditions: conn authenticated with raw key + valid witness header
expected_results: recall returns 200 with the memory ranked, scoped to the key's subject, and meta present

test_cases.name: Body-supplied tenant/subject is ignored; cross-subject read is impossible within a tenant
preconditions: {raw_a, key_a} = fixture(:api_key, tenant: tenant, role: :agent)  # distinct agent_id A
{raw_b, key_b} = fixture(:api_key, tenant: tenant, role: :agent)  # distinct agent_id B
as key_a: POST a memory; drain embedding
steps: as key_b: POST /api/v1/memory/recall with body %{query: "...", subject_id: <A>}
expected_results: the body subject_id is ignored; key_b's scope stays subject B
key_a's memory is never returned to key_b; no 500 and no existence leak

test_cases.name: Cross-tenant read is impossible and body tenant_id is ignored
steps: POST /api/v1/memory/recall as key with body %{query: "x", tenant_id: tenant_u.id}
expected_results: scope stays tenant_t; the tenant_u memory is never returned; the row a prior write created lands under tenant_t/subject-of-key regardless of body

test_cases.name: Superadmin can list across subjects; agent cannot
preconditions: memories exist under two different subjects in tenant
expected_results: agent's all_subjects request is ignored/403 — it sees only its own subject

test_cases.name: Custody-halted key cannot write memory
expected_results: rejected consistently with other write endpoints (same status/shape as a halted knowledge write)

technical_notes: Controller: LoopctlWeb.MemoryController; view: LoopctlWeb.MemoryJSON; routes in lib/loopctl_web/router.ex under the existing :authenticated scope "/api/v1" (superadmin oversight under /api/v1/admin or a role-gated param).
Model the controller on an existing write-capable knowledge controller for the plug pipeline + error envelope; do not invent a new auth path.

The scope struct passed to Loopctl.Memory is built from conn.assigns set by ResolveApiKey/SetTenant/Impersonate; subject_id per US-28.1 AC-28.1.4. Note Impersonate merges tenant/role onto the superadmin key — ensure the impersonated subject_id is resolved deterministically, not left as the superadmin's nil agent_id.
Keep recall a POST (query/params in body) to match knowledge_search ergonomics.
OpenAPI: operation macros go IN the controller (use OpenApiSpex.ControllerSpecs, as article_controller.ex ~line 15); only schemas live in lib/loopctl/api_spec/schemas.ex.
fixture(:api_key, tenant:, role:) returns {raw_key, %ApiKey{}} and already exists; there is no human-user fixture.
agent role is the floor (level 1) in lib/loopctl/auth/role.ex — 'role >= agent' is a no-op gate; the boundary is (tenant_id, subject_id).
